newsitem.title: GERMANY: German cabinet approves bill to ensure cattle cull.
newsitem.headline: German cabinet approves bill to ensure cattle cull.

text.p: The German cabinet on Wednesday approved a permanent order for the slaughter of cattle imported from Britain and Switzerland after an emergency decree on the issue ran into legal problems.
Agriculture Minister Jochen Borchert said the new order would replace the emergency measure, agreed after a new mad cow disease scare, which was ruled unlawful by several local courts.

The latest fears about bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE), or mad cow disease, were sparked in Germany last month after officials said they thought they had found the first German-born cow to die of the disease.

The discovery of the cow, thought to have been infected by its British mother, prompted federal and state agriculture ministries to agree to slaughter over 5,000 cattle from Britain and Switzerland -- the countries with the most native BSE cases.
The cow was the fifth to die of the disease in Germany.

But the origin of the cow was later cast into doubt, causing farmers to protest against the mass slaughter and consumer organisations to accuse Bonn of not exerting sufficient control over the import of animals and feed.

Several courts have ruled that the emergency decree, which circumvented parliament, was unnecessary because all cattle from Britain had already been registered and could not be slaughtered for meat or sold.

Genetic tests on the cow at the centre of the latest scare should be completed next month. If it is shown to have been infected by its mother, officials could order the cull of around 12,000 offspring of imported cattle.
The new order approved by the cabinet now needs the approval of both houses of parliame
